title: Mathematical Formalism of Functions
quickSummary: A function f: A → B satisfies Totality (every element in A has an image) and Single-Valuedness (no element in A has multiple images).
summary: Master the rigorous definition of functions, totality vs single-valuedness, arrow diagrams, and the geometric Vertical Line Test.

summaryBox.title: Function Criteria
summaryBox.takeaway: Totality: ∀x ∈ A, ∃y ∈ B such that (x, y) ∈ f. Single-valuedness: (x, y₁) ∈ f ∧ (x, y₂) ∈ f ⟹ y₁ = y₂.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
FUNCTION vs RELATION MAP
                         
       VALID FUNCTION (f: A ➔ B)               INVALID FUNCTION (Not a function)
       
       Set A          Set B                    Set A          Set B
       ┌───┐          ┌───┐                    ┌───┐          ┌───┐
       │ 1 ├─────────►│ a │                    │ 1 ├────┬────►│ a │ (1 maps to 2 elements)
       │ 2 ├─────┐    │ b │                    │ 2 │    └────►│ b │
       │ 3 ├────►└───►│ c │                    │ 3 │          │ c │ (3 has NO image!)
       └───┘          └───┘                    └───┘          └───┘
conceptBreakdown.content:
A **Function** (or Mapping) $f$ from set $A$ to set $B$, denoted $f: A \to B$, is a special relation $f \subseteq A \times B$ satisfying two non-negotiable structural conditions:

1. **Existence of Image (Totality)**: Every element $x \in A$ must be related to some element $y \in B$:
   $$\forall x \in A, \quad \exists y \in B \quad \text{such that } (x, y) \in f$$
2. **Uniqueness of Image (Single-Valuedness)**: No element $x \in A$ can be related to more than one element in $B$:
   $$\text{If } (x, y_1) \in f \quad \text{and} \quad (x, y_2) \in f, \quad \text{then } y_1 = y_2$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.1 The Vertical Line Test
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.1 The Vertical Line Test
conceptBreakdown.content:
### The Vertical Line Test (Geometric Criterion)
A curve in the $x$-$y$ plane represents the graph of a real function $y = f(x)$ if and only if **every vertical line $x = c$ (for $c \in \text{Dom}(f)$) intersects the curve at EXACTLY ONE point**.
- If any vertical line intersects the curve at two or more points (e.g. circle $x^2 + y^2 = r^2$), the relation fails single-valuedness and is not a function.
